# Pre-Implementation Checklist: Document Deletion Endpoint

**Purpose**: Author self-review, standard depth — validate the quality, clarity, completeness, and
consistency of this feature's requirements (spec.md, plan.md, research.md, data-model.md,
contracts/) before `/speckit-tasks` breaks them into implementation work. This checks whether the
requirements are well-written, not whether any code works.
**Created**: 2026-08-16
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) | [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context
and requirements. Focus: general requirements quality (broad sweep, not a single domain). Depth:
Standard. Audience/timing: author, pre-`/speckit-tasks`. All 16 items below were resolved on
2026-08-16 by amending spec.md and research.md — see the resolution note under each item for
exactly what changed.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is a requirement defined for what happens when a download of a document is already in
  progress at the moment that same document is deleted — as opposed to the already-covered case of
  a *different* document being unaffected? [Completeness, Gap, Spec Edge Cases]
  - **Resolved**: new Edge Cases bullet — resolved by ordinary read-committed atomicity (each of the
    download's single `SELECT` and the deletion's single `DELETE` is already atomic on its own, so
    whichever commits first fully determines the outcome for the other; no torn read is possible).
    Echoed in research.md Decision 5 as an explicit addendum.
- [x] CHK002 Is a requirement defined for whether deletion attempts, successful or failed, are
  logged for operational visibility — consistent with the structured-logging precedent feature 004
  established (FR-016) for its own pipeline — or is logging left entirely unaddressed at the
  requirements level? [Completeness, Gap]
  - **Resolved**: new **FR-011** — every deletion attempt (success, not-found, or failure) MUST be
    logged with the identifier and outcome; explicitly scoped as diagnostic logging, not an audit
    trail (cross-referenced from the Assumptions "no authentication" bullet).
- [x] CHK003 Is there a stated precondition that feature 003's `ON DELETE CASCADE` relationship is
  actually present in the deployed schema before this feature's implementation begins, the way a
  comparable schema dependency was made an explicit precondition in feature 004's own
  pre-implementation checklist? [Completeness, Dependency, Spec Key Entities]
  - **Resolved**: Key Entities section now states this explicitly as an implementation precondition,
    not merely background context. research.md Decision 5 adds a matching "Precondition, not
    assumption" note explaining exactly what would go wrong if the cascade were ever absent.

## Requirement Clarity & Measurability

- [x] CHK004 Is "search" in SC-002 and User Story 1's first acceptance scenario clearly scoped to
  the same schema-level vector-similarity check feature 003 already established, so a reader cannot
  mistake it for implying a new `/chat`-style endpoint this feature would need to build? [Clarity,
  Traceability, Spec §SC-002]
  - **Resolved**: SC-002 now names feature 003's schema-level similarity-search capability
    explicitly and states directly that no `/chat`-style endpoint is implied or required.
- [x] CHK005 Is "unexpected server-side failure" in FR-010 and the Clarifications entry precise
  enough to exclude "the document does not exist" from being misread as a qualifying failure case,
  or does distinguishing the two rely on the reader separately noticing the "valid, existing
  document" qualifier elsewhere in the same requirement? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010]
  - **Resolved**: FR-010 reworded so the scoping clause ("does name an existing document; the
    FR-005/FR-008 'not found' cases do not apply") now leads the requirement instead of being
    embedded mid-sentence.
- [x] CHK006 Can FR-006's "confirmed... clearly distinguishable from the not found outcome" be
  objectively verified as written, given the spec deliberately leaves the distinguishing mechanism
  itself to plan.md — or does the requirement need its own minimum testable signal stated at the
  spec level to avoid being unfalsifiable on its own? [Measurability, Spec §FR-006]
  - **Resolved**: FR-006 rewritten to require a single, structurally distinct signal separating all
    three outcomes (success, not found, failed) that a caller can tell apart without reading any
    human-readable text — testable without dictating the specific mechanism (still left to plan.md).

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK007 Does the Assumptions section's "no additional application-level locking or
  coordination is introduced for deletion" read consistently alongside FR-010's requirement for
  explicit failure detection and reporting, or could a reader interpret the two as being in tension
  (one implying minimal new logic, the other requiring it)? [Consistency, Spec Assumptions vs
  §FR-010]
  - **Resolved**: the Assumptions bullet now explicitly distinguishes the two concerns
    (coordination/locking vs. failure detection/reporting) and states they are complementary, not in
    tension.
- [x] CHK008 Are the three identifier-outcome cases that all collapse to "not found" (malformed,
  never issued, already deleted — FR-005/FR-008) stated with fully parallel, exhaustive wording, or
  could a reader infer a fourth, unaddressed case is silently out of scope rather than explicitly
  ruled in or out? [Consistency, Clarity, Spec §FR-005 vs §FR-008]
  - **Resolved**: FR-008 now states directly that the three cases are jointly exhaustive — no fourth
    "not found" variant exists for any identifier value a caller could supply.

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK009 Is it explicitly confirmed — not merely inferable by cross-reference to feature 004's
  FR-013 — that deleting a document and then immediately re-uploading a file with the identical
  original filename produces a wholly unrelated new document? [Coverage, Gap]
  - **Resolved**: new Edge Cases bullet states this directly, citing FR-013 as the governing rule
    rather than leaving it to inference.
- [x] CHK010 Does FR-005's "not even validly formatted" phrasing give enough guidance to distinguish
  a malformed-but-UUID-shaped string from a categorically different kind of malformed input (e.g.,
  an empty string, an excessively long string, or path-traversal-like input), or is "validly
  formatted" left undefined at the requirements level? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §FR-005]
  - **Resolved**: FR-005 now gives concrete examples (not a UUID, an empty string, a string
    containing characters that could never form a valid identifier).

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK011 Are there any performance or resource-consumption requirements defined for deleting a
  document with an unusually large number of chunks (the cascade's own cost), beyond SC-005's
  single-document 2-second target? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §SC-005]
  - **Resolved**: SC-005 now states explicitly that the 2-second target holds regardless of chunk
    count, since cost is dominated by a single indexed operation, not the number of chunks removed.
- [x] CHK012 Is a requirement defined for whether the deletion capability itself could be abused
  (e.g., rapid repeated delete requests against the whole corpus), or is this explicitly and
  deliberately left out of scope at this PoC phase rather than simply unaddressed? [Gap, Security]
  - **Resolved**: new Assumptions bullet — "No rate limiting or abuse protection" — states this is a
    deliberate scope boundary tied to the absence of caller identity, not an oversight.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK013 Is the "no authentication/authorization" assumption cross-checked against whether any
  other in-repo requirement (constitution, or a prior spec) implies a delete-time actor identity is
  needed for a future audit-trail feature — the same cross-check feature 004's own checklist applied
  to its upload-time equivalent? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]
  - **Resolved**: the "No authentication/authorization" bullet now states this cross-check
    explicitly and clarifies FR-011's logging is diagnostic only, never an audit trail.
- [x] CHK014 Is the dependency on feature 005's `DocumentNotFoundException`/404 pattern being reused
  (not reimplemented) stated as an explicit implementation precondition, or only as descriptive
  narrative within the Assumptions and Key Entities sections? [Dependency, Traceability]
  - **Resolved**: research.md Decision 3 now states this as an explicit precondition — `parseId` and
    `DocumentNotFoundException` (feature 005) MUST remain present and unchanged; tasks.md must treat
    them as reused dependencies, not artifacts this feature owns.

## Ambiguities, Gaps & Conflicts Needing Resolution

- [x] CHK015 Does the spec anywhere resolve whether a caller should retry automatically after a
  `deletion_failed`-style outcome (FR-010), or does it leave retry guidance entirely to a future
  contract layer with no signal at the requirements level? [Ambiguity, Gap, Spec §FR-010]
  - **Resolved**: FR-010 now states a caller MAY safely retry once the underlying condition has
    cleared, citing feature 004 FR-011's equivalent "valid input, processing failed" category as
    precedent. research.md Decision 6 adds a matching retry-semantics note.
- [x] CHK016 Is there a single, agreed source of truth in this feature's requirements for what
  "chunk" and "document" mean — relying entirely on feature 003's definitions by reference — with no
  risk of a reader assuming this feature silently redefines either term? [Consistency,
  Traceability, Spec Key Entities]
  - **Resolved**: Key Entities section now states directly that neither term is redefined here; both
    keep exactly feature 003's meaning.
